- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3) within 5 days, model often overshoots downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid premature correction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects downward; delay downward adjustment by 1–2 days or reduce magnitude.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.2), model often fails to mean-revert; apply a mild downward bias (−0.5 to −1.5%) to align with historical mean reversion patterns.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate in early periods (first 7–10 days) when sentiment is bullish; apply a 0.5–1.5% downward correction to early forecast points.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “bullish → bearish” transitions, model often misjudges reversal timing; delay forecast adjustment until sentiment confirms trend shift.
